steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Criminal courts deal with offences against the state; civil courts deal with disputes between individuals or organisations | Key Fact: The Magistrates' Court hears 95% of criminal cases — summary offences and either-way offences | Key Fact: The Crown Court hears indictable offences (serious crimes) and appeals from the Magistrates' Court | Key Fact: The High Court hears the most serious civil cases, divided into three divisions: Queen's Bench, Chancery and Family
